title: School meals: sentences that turn halfway
note: For early insight on fragments. An answer that opens like a deflection, a fair follow-up that opens with 'what about', a real whataboutism, and an answer that turns into an attack in its last clause.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Minister, how will you pay for free school meals for every child?

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: What I can tell you is that it will be paid for by closing the non-dom tax loophole, which raises 3 billion pounds.

turns.speaker: SHD
turns.text: And what about the 3 billion you already spent on tax cuts last year?

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: Under your government, school meals were cut in half.

turns.speaker: SHD
turns.text: That is simply not true, and you know it.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Minister, the question was about last year's tax cuts.

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: Those tax cuts were the right thing to do, we stand by them, and the meals will be paid for in full.

turns.speaker: MIN
turns.text: The meals are fully funded, and frankly the shadow minister should apologise for the chaos his party caused in our schools.
